To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the costs of climate change are driven by changes to the distribution of weather and expectations channels that capture the effects of changes in the distribution on current and past investments, that the expectations channels are not captured by studies that rely on time variation in weather, and that the expectations channels can be quantified by estimating the effects of forecasts and simulating the effects of climate change on forecasts.
1) the economic costs of climate change are likely to be larger than the estimates based on time series variation, and 2) the economic benefits of climate change are unlikely to offset these costs.

the economic costs of climate change are driven primarily by expectations channels, and that the costs of climate change will be larger than those estimated by studies that ignore expectations channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the impact of climate change on the economy.
the following question: how does climate change affect economic outcomes?
the economic effects of climate change and how they are influenced by expectations about climate change.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the economic effects of climate change are likely to be positive, but the uncertainty is large.
the economic impacts of climate change are likely to be positive, but the magnitude of the impacts will depend on a number of factors.
the economic costs of climate change depend on the distribution of weather, expectations, and the degree to which climate change alters the distribution of weather and expectations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
climate change will have substantial economic costs, but the magnitude of those costs is sensitive to the assumptions one makes.
climate change is likely to have large economic effects that will be driven by the expectations channel.
the costs of future warming will be higher than suggested by the literature that relies on time series variation alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expectations channels are large and important.
the economic consequences of climate change are much larger when expectations are accounted for.
the economic impacts of climate change are much larger when expectations are accounted for.
